fields.agent_or_rep: Agent — first name only, or "Your representative" when the sheet has none (the subject line)
fields.collected_on: Salesforce — the day the contract was collected for delivery (the delivery-update task); letter J only
fields.matured_on: policy admin — not on the portfolio sheet
fields.maturity_date: the intelligence sheet or policy admin — not on the portfolio sheet
fields.token: the send list — opaque, never a policy number
fields.segment: the send list — the letter's own key
fields.svc_docs: service-record.py — documents on their policies in the Log Book, checked and sent on by the document team
fields.svc_requests: service-record.py — Salesforce service tasks the branch team completed for them
fields.svc_reminders: service-record.py — premium reminders sent to them
fields.svc_birthday: service-record.py — the month of their last birthday note
fields.agent_name: Agent — the full name as the sheet spells it; letter T only, in the subject and the notice
fields.terminated_on: the send list — the date Guardian Life terminated the contract, from its own notice; letter T only

taps.question: My details have changed

letters.name: A policy has matured, or is about to
letters.subject: {{agent_or_rep}} has moved on. The money in your policy has not.
letters.preheader: The money is yours. We want it to reach you on time, with what comes next talked through.

tap_labels.urgent: I want an agent now. Let me tell you my concerns first

letters.send_note: Matured files first, then anything maturing within six months. The maturity date comes from policy admin, not the sheet; a blank date drops out of the strip. Most of this group is a phone call, and it is the one call nobody resents.

letters.name: In force — under two years
letters.subject: {{agent_or_rep}} has moved on. Your policy has not.
letters.preheader: Nothing about your cover has changed. Tell us how the start has been.

tap_labels.urgent: I want an agent now. Let me tell you my concerns first

letters.send_note: In force, and the client's longest-held policy is under two years old. The newest relationships, with the least built up: the letter is about service and a named person, and asks how the start has been.

letters.name: In force — two to three years
letters.subject: {{agent_or_rep}} has moved on. Your policy has not.
letters.preheader: Same policy, same premium, same beneficiaries. Your view on the first years, in two minutes.

tap_labels.urgent: I want an agent now. Let me tell you my concerns first

letters.send_note: In force, longest-held policy two to three years old. Early enough that life has usually moved on since the policy was bought: the letter asks what has changed.

letters.name: In force — three to five years
letters.subject: {{agent_or_rep}} has moved on. Your policy has not.
letters.preheader: Everything your policy has built is still yours. We would like your view.

tap_labels.urgent: I want an agent now. Let me tell you my concerns first

letters.send_note: In force, longest-held policy three to five years old. Value is building: the letter says it is still theirs and asks what they want next.

letters.name: In force — five to ten years
letters.subject: {{agent_or_rep}} has moved on. Your policy has not.
letters.preheader: Same cover, same premium, same beneficiaries. Tell us how we have done.

tap_labels.urgent: I want an agent now. Let me tell you my concerns first

letters.send_note: In force, longest-held policy five to ten years old. Starting again elsewhere would cost these clients most of what they have built: the letter says every year still counts.

letters.name: In force — ten years or more
letters.subject: {{agent_or_rep}} has moved on. Your policy has not.
letters.preheader: Every year of your cover is still yours. Your view matters most to us.

tap_labels.urgent: I want an agent now. Let me tell you my concerns first

letters.send_note: In force, longest-held policy ten years or more. Most of the fund value sits here: the letter thanks them first and asks for their view.

letters.name: In force — cover started again in the last three years
letters.subject: {{agent_or_rep}} has moved on. Your policy has not.
letters.preheader: A free check of what you hold today, what carried over, and who your policy pays.

tap_labels.urgent: I want an agent now. Let me tell you my concerns first

letters.send_note: In force, and a policy of theirs lapsed or was surrendered within six months before, or a year after, another began, the newest such start inside the last three years. The new cover is still inside its first three years: the letter offers a free check of the file and of who the policy pays, and asks nothing about how it happened.

letters.name: In force — cover started again, more than three years ago
letters.subject: {{agent_or_rep}} has moved on. Your policy has not.
letters.preheader: A free look at your file: what you hold, what carried over, and who your policy pays.

tap_labels.urgent: I want an agent now. Let me tell you my concerns first

letters.send_note: In force, with a policy that lapsed or was surrendered close to the start of another, more than three years ago. A long relationship with a break in it: the letter recognises the years, and offers the same free check of the file and of who the policy pays.

letters.name: Lapsed
letters.subject: {{agent_or_rep}} has moved on. Your policy may still hold value.
letters.preheader: A policy that stopped does not always stop being worth something.

tap_labels.urgent: I want an agent now. Let me tell you my concerns first

letters.name: A premium showing as due
letters.subject: {{agent_or_rep}} has moved on. A premium is showing as due.
letters.preheader: Already paid it? Tell us and we put the record right. Not yet? Nothing is lost.

tap_labels.pay: Set me up to pay Guardian Life directly

letters.send_note: More than sixty on the Days column, after the paid-to date is checked against cash and the deduction file. Direct bill first. The days outstanding and the projected lapse date are printed from the sheet, so one letter serves every band; the receiving agent calls anyone over 180 days within two days.

letters.name: Contract collected for delivery, never acknowledged
letters.subject: {{agent_or_rep}} has moved on. Has your policy contract reached you?
letters.preheader: Your policy is in force. We need to be sure the contract itself reached you.

tap_labels.urgent: I want an agent now. Let me tell you my concerns first

letters.send_note: From Salesforce: the contract was received at the branch for delivery (the delivery-update e-mail, whose date is collected_on) and no acknowledgement followed; the undelivered-script chase confirms most of them. Goes in the first wave, and the receiving agent delivers within the week.

letters.name: An application still in progress
letters.subject: {{agent_or_rep}} has moved on. Your application has not.
letters.preheader: The cover you applied for starts when the policy is issued. Whatever is still needed, we bring to you.
letters.send_note: From the pending list: underwriting incomplete, missing requirements, awaiting settlement. Cover is not in place until the policy is issued, so these go in the first wave and an agent is assigned at once; every file is read before the call.

letters.name: The agent's contract was terminated
letters.subject: Your Guardian Life agent {{agent_name}} is no longer with Guardian Life.
letters.preheader: Your policy is unaffected. Please read what has changed, and tell us if you have been contacted.

tap_labels.paid: I have paid a premium that is not showing
tap_labels.urgent: I want an agent now. Let me tell you my concerns first

letters.send_note: Every client on the book of an agent whose contract Guardian Life terminated, whatever they hold; the name and the date are read off the sheet (Agent, terminated_on). Goes before every other letter. The notice is in Guardian Life's own words and says nothing about why; Compliance reads it before the batch.

letters.name: The agent's contract was terminated: application still in progress
letters.subject: Your Guardian Life agent {{agent_name}} is no longer with Guardian Life. Let us finish your application.
letters.preheader: The cover you applied for starts when the policy is issued. Whatever is still needed, we bring to you.
letters.send_note: The terminated book's clients whose application is still in progress: the notice that the contract was terminated, then the application letter's own words and question, because cover is not in place until the policy is issued. Goes first of all, with T.
